content: 1. The initial dosage of methenamine/sodium acid phosphate (Uroqid-Acid No. 2, Utac) is two tablets taken orally every six hours, accompanied by liberal fluid intake. For maintenance, the dosage is reduced to one to two tablets taken orally every 12 hours. This medication should only be used after a urinary tract infection (UTI) has been eradicated with appropriate antibiotics. 2. Methenamine is indicated for the prophylaxis or suppression of chronic, recurrent UTIs when long-term therapy is required. Sodium acid phosphate acts as a urinary acidifier. 3. The safety and efficacy of sodium acid phosphate have not been fully established. Co-administration of sodium phosphate rectal and sodium acid phosphate is contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergism, which can increase the effects or toxicity of either agent. Such combinations are also known to cause electrolyte disturbances and hypovolemia. 4. Sodium acid phosphate can decrease the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This interaction may impair absorption, and concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron has been shown in animal studies to significantly reduce plasma levels. Human studies have not been conducted. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Sodium acid phosphate and potassium phosphates, when administered intravenously, both increase serum potassium levels. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 6. Sodium acid phosphate decreases the levels of amphetamine, dextroamphetamine, lisdexamfetamine, methamphetamine, and methylenedioxymethamphetamine by increasing renal clearance. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 7. Sodium acid phosphate decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline and sarecycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing of tetracyclines should be separated from these products. 8. Sodium acid phosphate can cause adverse effects such as dysuria, gastric upset, nausea, rash, diarrhea, stomach pain, and vomiting. 9. Methenamine is classified as Pregnancy Category C. It is excreted in human milk, and caution is advised during lactation as the risk to the infant cannot be ruled out. Sodium acid phosphate is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy, with controlled studies in pregnant women showing no evidence of fetal risk. 10. Methenamine is hydrolyzed in acidic urine to ammonia and formaldehyde, which are bactericidal agents. It does not convert to formaldehyde in serum. Sodium acid phosphate acts as a urinary acidifier and elicits an osmotic effect in the GI tract. 11. Methenamine has a half-life of 3-6 hours, is well absorbed, and is 10-30% hydrolyzed by gastric acid unless in an enteric-coated tablet. Its peak urine time for formaldehyde is two hours for hippurate salt and 3-8 hours for mandelate salt. It is metabolized by the liver (10-25%) and excreted in the urine (90%). Its onset of action is 1-3 hours, with a duration of 1-3 hours and a bioavailability of 66%. 12. The information provided is for general informational and educational purposes only.
